replies:
Good — final round prep, focused and practical. I’ll run a quick 10-point plan, give the top question types and one strong answer template you can adapt, then run a short mock: I’ll ask the first interview question now.
10-point final-round prep plan (what to do, in order)
1) Story polish: have 3 short stories (team deadline, problem solved, failure + learning) in CAR (Context, Action, Result) format with numbers where possible.
2) Fit narrative: 30–60s "Why IB / Why Lincoln International / Why this group" that ties your background to their deal focus and culture.
3) Resume walkthrough: pick 3 resume highlights to talk about in depth (what you did, impact, methods, tools).
4) Technical basics: be ready to walk through a DCF at a high level, comparables, and EBITDA adjustments; know basic accounting linkages (NI → cash flow).
5) Market / deal awareness: name 1–2 recent Lincoln deals or sector plays and say why they matter (ask if you want sources after).
6) Questions to ask them: two tactical (team structure, typical day) and two thoughtful (recent deal rationale, career progression).
7) Logistics: confirm interviewer names, rounds, time, format; plan a 3–5 minute closing pitch of your value.
8) Tone + culture: Lincoln emphasizes mid-market advisory and teamwork — show ownership, humility, client focus.
9) Mock practice: run 6–8 practice questions aloud, time answers to 1–2 minutes for behavioral, 2–4 for technical.
10) Brief checklist: bring paper, pen, printed resume, questions; have concise follow-up note ready to send within 24 hours.
Top question types you will face (and what they evaluate)
- Tell me about yourself / Walk me through your resume — fit and storytelling.
- Why investment banking / Why Lincoln International / Why this group — motivation & firm knowledge.
- Behavioral: teamwork under pressure, challenge/conflict, failure, leadership — structure & outcomes.
- Technical: valuation methods, accounting basics, valuation adjustments, simple math on the spot.
- Deal or market discussion: recent M&A trends or Lincoln-specific deals — commercial awareness.
- Fit questions about long hours, travel, client interaction — culture fit and stamina.

Model answers / templates you can adapt
1) "Tell me about yourself" (30–45s)
Start: one-line current role + one-line recent achievement.
Middle: 1–2 sentences on relevant skills (modeling, due diligence, client work) with an example.
Close: why Lincoln + this group and what you bring.
Example structure:
- "I'm [current role] at [employer], where I [one strong bullet—e.g., built 3 buy-side models that supported two acquisitions totaling $X]. I focus on financial modeling, due diligence, and client-facing analysis. In my last deal I led the LBO/valuation model that found a 20% upside and helped the team refine the investment case. I want Lincoln because of its mid-market focus in [sector] and its hands-on M&A advisory approach — I can contribute immediate modeling and deal-execution capacity while learning client strategy."
2) Behavioral story template (CAR) — Team under deadline
- Context (20s): what the project was and the deadline.
- Action (40–50s): your specific actions, trade-offs, tools, how you coordinated.
- Result (20s): measurable outcome, what you learned.

3) "Why Lincoln?" (45–60s)
- One sentence on firm strengths (mid-market, cross-border, sector focus).
- One sentence tie to your background or a deal: what you’ve done that fits.
- One sentence on mutual fit: what you’ll add and how you’ll grow.
Quick technical prep notes (must-know bullets)
- DCF: free cash flow = EBIT*(1-tax) + D&A - capex - ΔNWC; terminal value via Gordon or exit multiple; discount with WACC.
- Comps: EV/EBITDA and EV/Revenue, adjust for non-recurring items and differing fiscal calendars.
- Accounting link: NI → add back non-cash items → change in working capital → operating cash flow.
- Be ready to explain why EBITDA, not net income, for operating performance.
One short answer you can adapt — "Tell me about a time you worked with a team under a deadline"
Use CAR; here's a concise draft you can replace specifics in brackets:
- Context: "Last year I worked on a sell-side preparation where the client accelerated the timeline to three weeks to accept bids."
- Action: "I led the financial model cleanup: I re-built the historical P&L into a standardized template, reconciled adjustments with accounting, and coordinated with the associate to run sensitivity cases. I split tasks, set daily checkpoints, and produced a 3-scenario valuation pack."
- Result: "We delivered on time; two buyers advanced to final bids and the client closed at a price 12% above the initial expectation. I improved my stakeholder communication and learned to prioritize high-impact adjustments."

Now the mock: first question (answer aloud or type it, then I'll score and give one concrete improvement and the next question)
"Walk me through your resume / Tell me about yourself."

One question only: do you want the mock scored verbatim (I score exactly what you type) or do you want feedback on tone/structure only? Default: score verbatim.
items.note: The agent provided a clear, actionable final-round prep plan, templates, technical bullets, and a mock-question with scoring option—well-aligned with a finalist's needs.
